topic: Sharp action-dependent selective-label bounds for untrialed human-AI deployment. In a finite randomized multi-policy SCM, observe binary ground-truth Z only when endogenous action A reveals it, index common response potentials by distinct externally certified prediction-performance values q, and impose the Zhang-Skalnes-Chen-Oberst unit-level correctness, performance-order, and neutral restrictions. Define the Selective-Label Counterfactual-Correctness polytope over Z and q-indexed action/outcome response types; prove its two LP optima are attained sharp endpoints for the untrialed downstream mean, strictly refine the Z-blind projection on a nonempty relative-open set, and construct finite-sample whole-set inference by intersecting a simultaneous multinomial confidence polytope with the observable-law polytope. Use Euclidean projection for plug-in endpoints and derive projection-composed directional limits with valid m-out-of-n subsampling at simultaneous ties. Include the verified 32-type witness with full [1/2,3/4], blind [1/4,1], and the Imai PSA trial/aihuman consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Finite legal types give O=B(Delta) and every feasible weight vector canonically constructs an attaining SCM, so optimizing the untrialed-outcome coordinate yields the exact sharp interval. Independent enumeration reproduced the 32-type bounds and the relative-interior perturbation full [397/800,601/800] versus blind [99/400,1]. Checks covered same-q collisions, performance ties, empirical infeasibility, boundary laws, endpoint attainment, and classification-risk or policy-value relabeling; no prior-art collision survived. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove conservative conditional quantile validity for centered m-out-of-n subsampling of the joint projection-composed endpoint map when the observable law lies on a projection face and both LPs have multiple optimal bases, including atoms in the directional limit. EARLY KILL TEST: On the 32-type instance, choose a boundary law with simultaneous projection and endpoint ties, enumerate active cones and optimal dual faces, derive the exact Gaussian directional law, and compare centered subsampling for several m/n tending to zero; stop if conservative-quantile convergence fails.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the exact sharp interval for an untrialed policy's downstream mean when the binary correctness label is observed only under an endogenous revealing action, while retaining unit-level counterfactual-correctness, performance-order, and neutral-prediction restrictions.

source_refs.claim: The paper assumes ground-truth labels are fully observed for its main theorem, explicitly leaves more general missing-label structures to future work, and does not claim its counterfactual-correctness bounds are tight.
source_refs.author: Jonathan Zhang, Erik Skalnes, Jacob M. Chen, Michael Oberst
source_refs.venue: UAI / Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 337

source_refs.claim: The selective-label problem arises because outcomes such as failure to appear are observed only for defendants whom judges release.
source_refs.author: Himabindu Lakkaraju, Jon Kleinberg, Jure Leskovec, Jens Ludwig, Sendhil Mullainathan

source_refs.claim: The PSA framework evaluates human-alone, human-with-AI, and AI-alone systems but identifies selective-label comparisons only under its own baseline-potential-outcome restrictions.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael, D. James Greiner, Melody Huang, Kosuke Imai, Zhichao Jiang, Sooahn Shin
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

open_problems.why_unsolved: Zhang et al. separate the two obstacles that collide here: their main bounds condition on observed Z and are not asserted sharp because unit-level restrictions involve joint response potentials while their formulas optimize conditional means; their action-dependent missing-label experiment is explicitly described as possibly misspecified. Lakkaraju et al. establish that judicial actions generate precisely this nonrandom label observability but do not supply a causal sharp-set construction. The missing step is not a missing-at-random correction: one must enumerate action, label, and downstream-outcome response types jointly, impose the unit-level order restrictions before projection, and prove every feasible type mixture has an attaining SCM.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite response-type polytope theorem proving that its two LP values equal the sharp lower and upper endpoints for the untrialed downstream mean, together with an explicit observable law on which these endpoints strictly improve the Z-blind projection.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the closest motivation arc—updated models cannot each be trialed—and states both the missing-Z and sharpness boundaries that the new result resolves.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ML systems are repeatedly updated -> rerunning an RCT for every update is infeasible -> correctness and perceived performance can inform untrialed effects -> action-dependent missing truth requires a sharp selective-label identified set

method_exemplars.technique: Encode finite SCM response functions and incomplete observations as a polynomial program, reduce to an LP when observable and structural restrictions are linear, and certify sharpness by optimization over the complete latent-type simplex.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested object is a finite discrete causal model with selection and missing data; the response-type feasibility argument is the structural analogue of the desired attaining-SCM proof.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct calibrated projection confidence intervals by relaxing estimated moment constraints and repeatedly solving feasibility and endpoint programs, with uniform coverage over partially identified models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sharp interval is a scalar projection of a polyhedral identified set, so calibrated projection is a direct inference benchmark for the proposed whole-set confidence construction.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish conservative conditional-quantile validity—or give a sharp failure counterexample—for centered m-out-of-n subsampling of the joint Euclidean-projection-composed lower/upper LP endpoint map when the observable law is on a projection face, both LPs have multiple optimal bases, and the directional limit has atoms.

source_refs.claim: Directionally differentiable maps have non-Gaussian delta-method limits and generally invalidate the ordinary bootstrap; the paper develops derivative-aware resampling and treats convex-set projections.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang, Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: Direct bootstrap and m-out-of-n bootstrap confidence-interval endpoints can fail even asymptotically in simple moment-inequality models, so validity depends on the exact resampling construction.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews, Sukjin Han

source_refs.claim: Its asymptotic normality theorem imposes margin conditions separating competing extrema and performance values, thereby excluding simultaneous argmin/argmax and performance ties.
source_refs.author: Jonathan Zhang, Erik Skalnes, Jacob M. Chen, Michael Oberst
source_refs.venue: UAI / Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 337

source_refs.excerpt: Uniform coverage with simultaneous cut ties, near-active faces, and changing survivor support is explicitly open.
A proof of uniform tie-inclusive coverage and uniform level ... is still absent.
Replace the failure-only kernel with a new calibration or correction rule for the contact-gap endpoint

open_problems.why_unsolved: The statistic composes two nonsmooth maps: Euclidean projection onto an observable-law polytope and LP value maps whose derivatives optimize over lower and upper dual faces. Fang–Santos supplies the directional delta framework, but at simultaneous faces the piecewise-linear Gaussian limit may have atoms, where weak conditional convergence does not deliver quantile convergence. Andrews–Han show that centered m-out-of-n endpoint resampling can fail in moment-inequality models, while the prior failed intersection-bound proposal warns that a generic max-map failure is already known and asks for a positive calibration rule. The new work must therefore prove tie-inclusive conservativeness for this exact composed map or isolate a finite polyhedral failure regime.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving primitive cone/dual-face and m→∞, m/n→0 conditions under which centered subsampling critical values yield liminf simultaneous coverage at least 1−α for both endpoints at atomic limits, or a finite polyhedral Gaussian counterexample identifying the precise failure regime.

writing_exemplar.why: Its formulation moves from smooth delta-method intuition to bootstrap failure and valid inference for nonsmooth economic maps; the new paper can extend that arc to simultaneous projection and LP faces.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Plug-in inference normally uses smooth delta methods -> projection and LP values are only directionally differentiable -> ordinary bootstrap can fail -> simultaneous faces and atomic limits require a tailored subsampling theorem

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the functional directional delta method and estimate the full directional derivative rather than bootstrapping the original nonsmooth map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both projection and optimized endpoint maps are finite-dimensional Hadamard directionally differentiable transformations of an asymptotically Gaussian multinomial law.

method_exemplars.technique: Use numerical directional differentiation with a vanishing step size to approximate a computable convex Lipschitz map's nonsmooth limit law without selecting one active basis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The projection-composed endpoint map is computable but its common active-cone derivative is cumbersome; a numerical derivative can reproduce the face-dependent map.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove uniform subsampling and m-out-of-n validity through test-statistic formulations designed for discontinuous moment-inequality limits.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the positive counterpart to Andrews–Han's endpoint failure and shows that conservativeness must be proved through the statistic and acceptance region, not inferred from m/n→0 alone.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive a sharp violation-budget sensitivity region for untrialed selective-label impact when at most a specified mass of units may violate counterfactual correctness, performance ordering, or performance-invariant neutrality.

source_refs.claim: The paper notes that expectation-level falsification tests cannot detect all unit-level violations and explicitly calls for handling reversals of performance ordering and performance-dependent neutral actions.
source_refs.author: Jonathan Zhang, Erik Skalnes, Jacob M. Chen, Michael Oberst
source_refs.venue: UAI / Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 337

source_refs.claim: Breakdown-frontier analysis indexes relaxations of identifying assumptions and provides inference for the boundary where a causal conclusion ceases to hold.
source_refs.author: Matthew A. Masten, Alexandre Poirier

source_refs.claim: A mean-outcome sensitivity model yields sharp risk-assessment bounds and doubly robust estimation when selective historical decisions may be confounded.
source_refs.author: Ashesh Rambachan, Amanda Coston, Edward H. Kennedy

open_problems.why_unsolved: Hard unit-level restrictions exclude every violating response type, although Zhang et al. emphasize that observable falsification tests operate only in expectation and can miss individual violations. A violation-budget extension changes the first proof step from deleting illegal types to retaining them with separate linear mass constraints for correctness, order, and neutrality failures. Masten–Poirier provide the breakdown-frontier logic and Rambachan–Coston–Kennedy provide risk-assessment sensitivity machinery, but neither handles these three human-trust restrictions under action-dependent selective labels.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A parametric LP characterization of the sharp endpoint surface over three violation budgets, including the minimal budget needed to reverse a specified deployment conclusion and a simultaneous confidence band for that breakdown surface.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames sensitivity through a decision-relevant frontier rather than an arbitrary collection of robustness checks.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Credible identifying restrictions may fail for some units -> binary maintain/drop analysis hides robustness -> index the permitted failures quantitatively -> locate where the untrialed-policy conclusion breaks down

method_exemplars.technique: Define a nested relaxation family, derive the conclusion region in sensitivity-parameter space, and characterize its boundary as a breakdown frontier.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Mass budgets on violating response types generate a nested family of sharp polytopes whose endpoint inequalities directly define a frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate sharp risk and performance bounds with influence-function pseudo-outcomes and sample splitting, then propagate them through sensitivity-indexed optimization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest estimation literature for decision-induced missing outcomes and predictive-performance bounds, though its sensitivity parameter governs confounding rather than unit-level trust restrictions.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the jointly sharp image of the selective-label response-type polytope for untrialed downstream mean, classification risk, and policy value, rather than relying on separate scalar relabeling bounds.

source_refs.excerpt: Extend the attainment construction to a jointly sharp vector of benefit, no-harm, and large-gain tier events
Each endpoint has a representing measure, and hence a compatible hierarchical SCM

open_problems.why_unsolved: The same latent type weights must realize all three deployment functionals simultaneously. Separate coordinatewise LP endpoints—even if each has an attaining SCM—need not paste into one common SCM, so scalar relabeling checks establish marginal sharpness but not the vector region. The first changed proof step is to replace one exposed endpoint face by the complete support-function family of the three-dimensional polytope image and construct a common attaining model for every exposed point.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact H- or V-representation, or equivalently a finite support-function characterization, of the three-target identified polytope with a common-SCM attainment theorem and a simultaneous confidence-region construction obtained from the multinomial confidence polytope.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its multi-measure benefit/no-harm motivation while emphasizing that selective observation makes a common latent-law region—not separate intervals—the decision-relevant object.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Deployment decisions depend on several causal performance criteria -> each criterion is only partially identified under selective labels -> one common policy requires their jointly attainable region

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a finite response-function polytope and evaluate support-function LPs for multiple linear causal queries.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired object is the linear image of one finite response-type feasibility polytope, so support functions give a statement-level joint characterization and common attainment.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert simultaneous finite-sample tests for a mixing law and propagate the resulting confidence set to several target functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Intersecting a multinomial confidence region with the observable-law polytope and mapping it through all three coordinates is the finite-response analogue of exact set propagation.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend sharp untrialed-policy bounds from binary recommendations and actions to finite ordinal or multiclass recommendations and actions, preserving error-type-specific correctness orders rather than reducing the system to binary buckets.

source_refs.claim: The paper binarizes the PSA's ordinal risk scores and bail actions for simplicity and names continuous recommendations and more efficient alternatives to bucketing as future work.
source_refs.author: Jonathan Zhang, Erik Skalnes, Jacob M. Chen, Michael Oberst
source_refs.venue: UAI / Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 337

source_refs.claim: The paper explicitly identifies nonbinary decisions and outcomes as a future methodological extension of its human–AI evaluation framework.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael, D. James Greiner, Melody Huang, Kosuke Imai, Zhichao Jiang, Sooahn Shin
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

source_refs.claim: Sharp bounds for ordinal potential-outcome comparisons can be obtained with linear programming and stochastic-order restrictions.
source_refs.author: Jiannan Lu, Peng Ding, Tirthankar Dasgupta
source_refs.venue: Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics

open_problems.why_unsolved: Binarization collapses substantively different PSA scores, bail levels, and error types, although the source application has integer risk scores and multiple bail actions. The first proof step must replace binary correct/incorrect types with multiclass confusion-category and ordinal-action response maps, then determine which performance orders remain coherent when errors have direction and magnitude. Existing ordinal-outcome LP bounds do not include an untrialed algorithm, endogenous human mediation, or action-dependent label revelation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite multiclass response-type formulation with necessary and sufficient linear order restrictions, sharp LP bounds for a specified ordinal policy-value or classification-loss target, and a theorem quantifying when coarse binary aggregation strictly enlarges the identified set.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation and PSA application naturally expose the gap between the genuinely ordinal decision problem and binary methodological abstractions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Humans remain final decision-makers in high-stakes AI systems -> performance must compare human-alone, assisted, and AI-alone rules -> the PSA consumer contains ordinal scores and actions -> sharp multiclass selective-label evaluation is needed

method_exemplars.technique: Encode ordinal potential-outcome margins and stochastic-order restrictions in an LP and prove the extrema are sharp for benefit-type causal estimands.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its ordered-category coupling problem is the nearest finite analogue for replacing binary correctness with direction-sensitive multiclass response types.

method_exemplars.technique: Automate discrete response-function enumeration and certify sharp bounds under selection, missingness, and custom causal restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination remains finite but its type space grows rapidly; automated response-function construction prevents an ad hoc binary-only derivation.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate projection confidence intervals for smooth scalar functionals of moment-inequality identified sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Multiclass cell probabilities still yield a finite multinomial moment model whose policy-value endpoint is a projection of the enlarged polytope.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize sharp bounds for a newly introduced human–AI policy in a finite-horizon deployment where recommendations, endogenous actions, selectively revealed labels, and downstream outcomes recur over time and current actions alter later label availability.

source_refs.claim: The paper explicitly lists dynamic settings with multiple decisions and outcomes observed over time as a future extension.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael, D. James Greiner, Melody Huang, Kosuke Imai, Zhichao Jiang, Sooahn Shin
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

source_refs.claim: Dynamic regime welfare can be partially ordered sharply by constructing LP bounds over history-indexed latent response states.
source_refs.author: Sukjin Han
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: A static type records one recommendation, action, label, and outcome response; with repeated deployment the revealing action changes the future observed history and possibly the human's trust in later models. The first proof step must replace static types with nonanticipating history-indexed response maps and express correctness and performance restrictions conditional on reachable histories. Han's dynamic LP machinery addresses partially ordered regime welfare under endogeneity, but not selectively observed correctness labels, model-performance-indexed trust, or extrapolation to an untrialed AI policy.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-horizon response-history polytope whose LP extrema are proved sharp for cumulative untrialed-policy value, plus a characterization of when periodwise sharp intervals fail to compose into the sharp dynamic interval.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly motivates empirical evaluation of human–AI systems and explicitly lands on repeated decisions and outcomes as the destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: One-shot experiments compare human and AI decision systems -> deployed systems repeatedly update recommendations and actions -> current actions determine which truths become observable -> dynamic selective-label policy value requires its own sharp identified set

method_exemplars.technique: Represent dynamic potential decisions and outcomes by latent history-response states, solve pairwise welfare-gap LPs, and prove sharp partial ordering of regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same history-indexed latent-state machinery can host selective revelation and performance-order restrictions while targeting cumulative untrialed-policy welfare.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate a discrete causal model with incomplete observations into an optimization over response functions and certify sharpness during computation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Dynamic histories cause combinatorial type growth, making automated response-function generation and certified optimization especially valuable.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct uniformly valid calibrated projection intervals by optimizing over relaxed sample moment constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The cumulative value remains a scalar projection of a finite moment-inequality model, although the dynamic response polytope is larger.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether the q-ordered selective-label endpoint LP admits an exact threshold/min-cut representation and strongly polynomial algorithm, or exhibit a smallest legal correctness/order/neutral instance proving that no Ferrers-network reduction preserves both endpoints.

source_refs.excerpt: The tie-safe capacity projection, three-branch threshold min-cut equality, full-law endpoint attainment
No magnitude-independent threshold-flow algorithm for the survivor-complier partial-transport problem.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The donor construction works because an ordered strict-benefit event induces a Ferrers graph with nested cuts. In the selective-label model, q-order, unit correctness, neutrality, and endogenous reveal decisions jointly constrain Z-indexed response types; it is unknown whether their incidence matrix still reduces to nested capacities. The first proof step that changes is establishing total unimodularity or network representability of the selective-label constraint matrix rather than the donor partial-transport matrix.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an explicit lower/upper threshold-cut formula with a strongly polynomial flow algorithm and endpoint-attaining SCM construction for every feasible law, or a minimal certified legal instance whose LP face lattice contradicts any nested-cut representation.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its problem arc from categorical SCM response functions to reproducible tight bounds, then pose symbolic tractability under q-order as the bottleneck.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Categorical SCMs yield finite latent response types -> LPs give sharp but opaque bounds -> q-order may expose a combinatorial cut formula and scalable computation

method_exemplars.technique: Use symbolic response-function elimination for finite ordinal causal-benefit bounds and derive explicit finite-category formulas.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems impose order on finite response types; the selective-label target asks whether that order upgrades generic LP elimination to a threshold-flow representation.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct finite response-function LPs with observable-probability constraints and repeatedly evaluate their endpoints under resampled laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the computational baseline the strongly polynomial selective-label evaluator would replace while preserving the same sharp endpoint object.

literature_map:
1. Zhang, Skalnes, Chen, and Oberst (2026, UAI; arXiv:2607.21806) is the closest anchor: it bounds untrialed-model impact using unit-level correctness and performance-dependent trust.
2. Its main theorem assumes Z observed, explicitly leaves richer missing-Z mechanisms open, and expressly does not claim tightness of its counterfactual-correctness bounds.
3. Its inference theorem requires margin separation, excluding the simultaneous performance and endpoint ties central to the proposed boundary analysis.
4. Chen and Oberst (2025, UAI; arXiv:2502.09467) establish the preceding 'trial once' framework based on deterministic predictions and performance-mediated trust.
5. Lakkaraju, Kleinberg, Leskovec, Ludwig, and Mullainathan (2017, KDD; DOI 10.1145/3097983.3098066) formulate selective labels and use decision-maker heterogeneity rather than a sharp SCM identified set.
6. Kleinberg et al. (2018, QJE; NBER DOI 10.3386/w23180) show why bail-policy evaluation is counterfactual: crime outcomes are unavailable for detained defendants.
7. Imai et al. (2023, JRSS-A; DOI 10.1093/jrsssa/qnad010) supply the randomized PSA trial and principal-stratification consumer.
8. Ben-Michael et al. (2025, PNAS; arXiv:2403.12108) compare human-alone, assisted, and AI-alone systems and explicitly call for nonbinary and dynamic extensions.
9. Rambachan, Coston, and Kennedy (2022; arXiv:2212.09844) derive sharp sensitivity bounds and doubly robust inference for counterfactual risk assessments under unmeasured confounding.
10. Duarte et al. (2024, JASA; arXiv:2109.13471) show that discrete SCMs with selection and missingness reduce to response-function polynomial programs, with LPs as an important special case.
11. Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018; arXiv:1507.01542) give sharp ordinal-outcome bounds, a natural donor for multiclass recommendation/action extensions.
12. Han (2024, JASA; arXiv:1912.10014) obtains sharp partial welfare orderings for dynamic regimes through history-indexed LPs, but does not include selective labels or human–AI trust.
13. Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud; arXiv:1404.3763) provide the directional delta method and bootstrap-failure theory for nonsmooth maps, including convex projections.
14. Hong and Li (2018, Journal of Econometrics; DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2018.06.007) provide a numerical directional delta method for computable convex Lipschitz maps.
15. Andrews and Han (2009, Econometrics Journal; DOI 10.1111/j.1368-423X.2008.00265.x) show direct centered bootstrap and m-out-of-n endpoint inference can fail, while Andrews and Guggenberger (2009; DOI 10.1017/S0266466608090257), Hsieh, Shi, and Shum (2022; DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.06.001), and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019; arXiv:1601.00934) provide alternative test, optimizer, and calibrated-projection routes.
prior_proposal_map:
A bounded filename/content index covered 2,104 eligible proposal cores, rejected angles, reviewer JSONs, bank READMEs, and writeups under doc/research.
The closest active source was pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport/v1: its proto_core leaves uniform face-aware inference open, and angle0_v2/v3 request a specified Euclidean projection, calibrated critical values, and joint-vector sharpness.
The downgraded pid_datafusion_exact_compatibility/v1 proto_core independently leaves tie-inclusive uniform coverage/level open for a numerical directional-delta construction.
The failed pid_bound_intersection_inference/v1 angle1 archive and reviewer were inspected; they show that a plain max-map derivative or naive-bootstrap failure is already Fang–Santos territory and demand a positive new calibration rule.
The active scm_finiteplate_bernstein_ate_bounds/v1 core and angle0_v5 review were mined for boundary-fiber stratification, exact certificates, endpoint-SCM attainment, and confidence-set inversion.
The downgraded pid_multivalued_iv_vertex_calculus/v1 core and reviews were mined for exact dual activity signatures, nonsimple-vertex obstacles, and adjacency-atlas methods.
No earlier proposal directly treats action-dependent selective labels, certified q-indexed response types, or the Imai PSA human-AI consumer; the strongest reuse is therefore inferential/combinatorial technique transfer rather than duplicate-kernel recovery.
